title: System One: the trailer
summary: A one-minute tour of the free System One course on decision models.

scenes.narration: Ask a language model a simple question in your code, and it writes an answer one token at a time, which you then parse, and hope. A decision model reads your data once and scores every allowed answer. Same question, a quarter of a second.
You send your data and typed questions: a yes or no, a choice from your options, a score on your scale. Back comes a typed answer for each one, with a probability, all at once.

scenes.narration: And the probabilities mean something. On real banking messages, Jev was eighty percent right overall, but ninety six percent right on the half it was surest about. Automate those, and send the rest to a person.
They're not magic. Ask one to count the fruits in a list of twelve words, and it says five. There are six. The course shows you where they break, and how to keep that work in code.

scenes.narration: And it's cheap enough to ask everything. Thirteen questions in one request took a quarter of a second. Three thousand messages cost twenty two cents.
System One. A free course on decision models, built from a hundred ninety nine sources and fourteen thousand API calls of our own. And your coding agent can take it too.
